summary: In Greek mythology, Dolops (Ancient Greek: Δόλοψ) was an Achaean leader, son of Clytius, whom Hector slew when Zeus vouchsafed the Trojan prince glory in his rampage of Iliad 11 — distinct from Dolops son of Lampus at Troy and from other mythic namesakes.

sections.heading: Slain in Hector's rampage
paragraphs: Homer asks who first and who last fell to Hector when Zeus granted him glory, and names Dolops son of Clytius among the Danaan leaders cut down with Asaeus, Autonous, Opites, Opheltius, Agelaus, Aesymnus, Orus, and Hipponous. After those captains Hector turned upon the multitude.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This atlas entry (dolops-clytiid) is the Achaean son of Clytius. Distinct from Dolops the Trojan, son of Lampus (dolops-trojan); from Dolops son of Cronus and Philyra, brother of Chiron; from Dolops son of Hermes, whose Magnesian tomb the Argonauts honoured; and from Dolops of Lemnos, father of the shepherd who tended Philoctetes.
